column3: Visual organisation of concurrent terminal and agent work with durable placement and grouping.
column10: Turn keeps the navigable tree and one selected WorkSurface authoritative instead of adopting a spatial topology authority.

column3: Selection opens the exact terminal, agent, resource or project content without duplicating its runtime.
column10: The source demonstrates distinct content surfaces; the canonical selection contract preserves the useful view-switching behavior.

column3: Terminal processes remain attached to durable sessions across view unmount and application restart.
column10: Warm process continuity is essential for unattended agentic work.

column3: Saved work recovers after UI restart, daemon restart, disconnect and host reboot with truthful continuity labels.
column10: Recovery is retained while Turn distinguishes reattachment from cold reconstruction.

column3: Shells, TUIs, services and logs retain complete terminal behavior alongside agent-aware processes.
column10: Generic terminal work is a first-class workload rather than an agent fallback.

column3: Agent nodes expose status, transcript, task, children, context, result and safe controls.
column10: Semantic agent information is retained in a unique WorkSurface.

column3: Groups form a recursively nestable, cycle-free hierarchy with stable order and explicit reparent semantics.
column10: Recursive organisation is required to scale beyond a flat list.

column3: A group can bind its descendants to an exact repository worktree without changing runtime ancestry.
column10: Turn models this as a typed CheckoutScopeBinding on a Session group and never lets it occupy primary main.

column3: A bounded note resource can be reviewed and linked as explicit agent context.
column10: Useful operator-authored briefs are preserved without turning content into authority.

column3: Files open in a first-class editor with revision-aware atomic save and conflict recovery.
column10: Editing remains bound to the exact file backend, root and target.

column3: Repository changes and diffs are inspectable without starting or mutating a runtime.
column10: Diff inspection belongs to the selected repository scope.

column3: Static web previews, interactive browsing and video are distinct isolated resource capabilities.
column10: Turn separates inert preview from interactive navigation and applies explicit storage and download policy.

column3: Dropped or pasted media becomes a bounded inert resource rather than executable workspace input.
column10: Media import is retained with size, type and persistence boundaries.

column3: Toolbar, palette and context actions share one searchable creation and command catalogue.
column10: One catalogue supports fast keyboard and pointer workflows without divergent defaults.

column3: Creation, navigation, close, search, panels and settings expose discoverable keyboard paths.
column10: Keyboard completeness is required for high-volume operation and accessibility.

column3: Reversible presentation mutations have deterministic undo and redo semantics under revisioned state.
column10: Turn preserves reversible organisation while applying canonical multi-client conflict rules.

column3: Workspace organisation, selection and recoverable resources persist without implicitly launching work.
column10: Saved presentation is data; restoration never fabricates runtime authority.

column3: First run can create a new workspace or open an existing local directory with bounded preflight.
column10: The onboarding path is brought into the shared catalogue and receipt model.

column3: A repository can be cloned into a reviewed destination with idempotent progress and partial-failure recovery.
column10: Clone is treated as an explicit operation rather than an opaque setup side effect.

column3: An SSH target can be adopted as a workspace after identity, root, capability and credential preflight.
column10: Remote onboarding never falls back to a same-named local path.

column3: Repository publication is an explicit previewed operation with remote, branch and credential receipts.
column10: Publish stays separate from create and is never automatic or remotely delegated.

column3: Captured task or output may propose a bounded safe alias while manual names always win.
column10: Turn separates local presentation aliases from provider conversation identity and title mutation.

column3: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Grok have dedicated versioned adapter identities.
column10: The complete measured roster enters one capability matrix instead of provider branches in core or UI.

column3: Operator-declared agents use the generic adapter contract and cannot acquire unproved semantics.
column10: Custom commands remain useful while unsupported capabilities stay explicit.

column3: Agent availability, version, launch modes and integration mechanisms are discovered and degrade independently.
column10: Capability evidence is reported per adapter, version, target and mechanism.

column3: Provider-specific hook dialects reduce into one versioned lifecycle and topology observation contract.
column10: Structured observations are retained without leaking provider branches beyond adapters.

column3: Working, waiting, blocked, done and interrupted evidence survives reconnect and resolves deterministically.
column10: Turn keeps process lifecycle and turn state separate while routing both consistently.

column3: Subagents are discovered as stable recursive children with causal parent and attempt identity.
column10: Subagents become canonical navigable nodes rather than transient cards.

column3: A subagent exposes bounded transcript, timing, task and result even when it owns no PTY.
column10: Semantic activity remains visible independently of terminal attachment.

column3: Per-conversation context use is shown with known units, window and freshness rather than guessed percentages.
column10: Context consumption remains distinct from billing quota.

column3: Account usage connectors cover Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Grok, Kimi and MiniMax with independent scope and failure.
column10: Additional quota providers enrich AccountProfile telemetry without falsely becoming runtime adapters.

column3: Several isolated authenticated provider profiles can coexist and launch exact frozen account bindings.
column10: Profile roots and credentials remain isolated from active instances and one another.

column3: Requested and effective model, approval mode, flags, cwd, target and worktree are visible per attempt.
column10: Launch configuration is telemetry with provenance, not an inferred label.

column3: A scoped model endpoint can route supported agents through an operator-owned credential reference and explicit model mapping.
column10: Gateway health, endpoint identity, TLS and effective launch receipt are modeled as a separate capability.

column3: Provider history can be searched and paged by exact profile and target without implicit launch or adoption.
column10: Inventory coverage and ownership remain explicit and private.

column3: A saved provider conversation may resume through a capability-gated native operation with continuity evidence.
column10: Resume is distinct from restart, attach and portable handoff.

column3: A supported conversation can branch while preserving source and new lineage identities.
column10: Turn labels provider branch, continuation and portable derivation separately.

column3: One agent can pull bounded transcript context from another through an explicit revocable grant.
column10: Cross-agent context transfer never implies control or ancestry.

column3: A reviewed digest and exact recent tail can move work between different agent adapters with a delivery receipt.
column10: Portable handoff is budgeted and does not claim native conversation continuity.

column3: Agents can exchange bounded typed messages through durable queues and independent delivery receipts.
column10: Messaging remains asynchronous and cannot become hidden synchronous joins or control.

column3: An operator or bounded flow can create several role-labelled agents and retain each independent result.
column10: Fan-out and verification are modeled as versioned Flow runs rather than presentation-only teams.

column3: Provider-native loops, schedules and background jobs have stable identity, iterations and independent controls.
column10: Native job truth remains distinct from Turn Flow recurrence.

column3: An agent may create and organise bounded resources through typed capability endpoints with durable receipts.
column10: Direct presentation control is replaced by least-privilege domain operations; prose output never becomes authority.

column3: Conversation title reading and provider rename are separately discovered, fenced and receipted.
column10: Either operation may degrade without inventing the other.

column3: Operator interruption is ordered from actionable evidence rather than visual placement or terminal output polling.
column10: Turn elevates this behavior into the sole routing authority across every surface.

column3: Agent running, input-required and completed states produce consistent badges, unread state and timing.
column10: Typed demands remain distinct from lifecycle and heuristic status.

column3: A permission or question can be answered against its exact interaction revision and remains pending until provider evidence closes it.
column10: Remote answers use an additional single-use grant; raw terminal input cannot spoof a typed response.

column3: Actionable changes can notify the operator outside the window without resolving or acknowledging them.
column10: Notifications route back through the same canonical Attention target.

column3: A compact desktop projection shows urgent agent state and routes to the canonical demand.
column10: The compact surface is a projection and never a second queue.

column3: Background and headless processes can send deduplicated privacy-bounded Attention push envelopes.
column10: Push acceptance, delivery, read and demand resolution stay separate states.

column3: Device notification grants are scope-bound, expiring, revocable and resilient to dead tokens and offline clients.
column10: A grant carries exact workspace, demand-kind, privacy and rate policy.

column3: A companion can project account usage and a bounded recent activity inbox with truthful coverage.
column10: Absence, partial pages and errors never appear as zero usage or no activity.

column3: A headless host observes local hooks and sends outbound notifications without opening an inbound control port.
column10: Loopback observation and outbound-only delivery preserve the zero-listener deployment boundary.

column3: Automatic focus defers during typing, alternate-screen input, modal work and voice review without dropping the demand.
column10: Attention remains available through one explicit next action when focus transfer would disrupt the operator.

column3: On-device speech capture and inference run outside the control plane and never use a cloud fallback.
column10: Local voice input is retained with a crash-isolated least-privilege worker.

column3: Transcription produces an editable memory-only draft that is inserted or sent only by the foreground operator.
column10: Voice never auto-submits and cannot retarget after capture.

column3: Speech models have explicit install, digest, size, licence, offline-use and deletion lifecycle.
column10: The optional model is inventoried separately from sessions and workspaces.

column3: A self-hosted browser surface uses the same hierarchy, terminal, repository and Attention protocols.
column10: The full surface preserves revisions and recovery while withholding desktop-only authority.

column3: Remote runtimes, files and repositories remain bound to an authenticated host generation and exact root.
column10: No remote outage may produce a same-name local effect.

column3: Companion pairing establishes revocable end-to-end encrypted device identity with replay protection.
column10: Remote transport is authenticated and key rotation or revocation is explicit.

column3: Collaborators can expose bounded presence and selection without granting input or control authority.
column10: Presence is optional, encrypted where shared and operationally non-authoritative.

column3: An authenticated full remote surface may create ordinary work, navigate views and type under an exact input lease.
column10: Permitted remote operations use the same typed mutation and revision protocol as desktop.

column3: Destructive lifecycle, provider deletion, external close, repository publication, secrets, trust and authority stay desktop-foreground-only.
column10: Turn deliberately keeps a stronger safety boundary while retaining ordinary remote creation, viewing and input.

column3: Repository status supports stage, unstage, discard, branch, commit, sync and push with exact scope and consequences.
column10: Source-control operations are first-class target-bound tools.

column3: Worktree creation, reconciliation and assignment support concurrent agent-per-branch work without locking primary main.
column10: Isolation is strengthened into a mandatory writer invariant.

column3: Repository hosting authentication and issue operations use an explicit credential seam with isolated failures.
column10: Credentials are referenced, redacted and never inherited as ambient content authority.

column3: A board projects live sessions with columns, priority, due date, assignees and comments over canonical identities.
column10: The board remains an optional projection and never a second runtime or topology authority.

column3: External issue cards retain source identity and support conflict-aware move, close and reopen reconciliation.
column10: External state is mapped through a rate-limited credential-isolated WorkItemSource.

column3: A workspace file explorer navigates and edits only the selected target and root.
column10: Remote and local paths share one file capability without fallback across targets.

column3: Commit history, graph and changed files are inspectable within the exact repository boundary.
column10: History inspection is read-only until a separate typed repository operation is chosen.

column3: A configured local agent may propose a commit message from a bounded staged diff without executing repository changes.
column10: Generated text remains a reviewed suggestion from a declared tool capability.

column3: Host memory totals, availability, swap and pressure are reported per exact execution target with freshness and coverage.
column10: Unknown or failed collection never appears as zero and remote targets never use local data.

column3: Process-tree memory is attributed to runtime attempts and nodes while closed owners and unmatched survivors remain visible.
column10: Stable process identity, shared-runtime buckets and partial coverage prevent double counting or invented splits.

column3: Live handles unmatched to current attempts are recoverable as target-scoped inventory with exact adopt, ignore or terminate actions.
column10: Orphans and survivors remain evidence without fabricated nodes.

column3: Multiple viewers can attach while one explicit revisioned lease owns input and resize.
column10: Concurrent input can never interleave silently.

column3: Usage, reset windows and recent account activity are projected per exact provider profile and target.
column10: Independent freshness and coverage preserve truthful multi-account telemetry.

column3: File upload and download use reviewed target-bound tickets, confinement and bounded transfer state.
column10: Transfers cannot escape the selected root or acquire execution authority.

column3: Application updates are discovered, staged and applied through an explicit platform-aware lifecycle.
column10: Update availability never blocks generic terminal use and installation remains a reviewed action.

column3: Bounded product announcements are shown without masquerading as operational Attention.
column10: News and setup guidance remain separate from the canonical interruption queue.

column3: Decorative mascot and pet presentation unrelated to operational state or control.
column10: The coverage ledger records the visible feature, but Turn excludes it because it adds no operator-control capability.

column3: The active terminal or text surface supports bounded find navigation without consuming terminal input.
column10: Search is a view operation and never mutates the selected runtime or acknowledges Attention.

column3: Terminal, note and editor content can switch to a sanitised markdown projection without changing source data.
column10: Rendered content remains an inert view with explicit unsupported and unsafe-content handling.

column3: Board mutations and comments expose an ordered activity history tied to canonical work identities.
column10: Activity history is evidence for a projection, not a second event or runtime authority.

column3: Terminal font, theme, contrast, zoom and preview settings preserve readable keyboard-operable output.
column10: Appearance controls are retained within the accessibility contract and cannot obscure semantic status.
